verses.text: “People say, ‘If a man sends his wife away and she leaves him and marries someone else, should he go back to her?’ Wouldn’t that leave the whole land filthy? But you’ve sold yourself to lover after lover. Even so, come back to me,” says the LORD.

“Look up at those bare hills! Is there anywhere you haven’t slept with someone? You sat at the roadside waiting for them like an Arabian in the wilderness. You’ve dirtied the land with your prostitution and your evil.
That’s why the showers stayed away and the late rain never came. Still, you wore a prostitute’s brazen look and refused to be ashamed.
Won’t you call out to me now, ‘My Father, you’re the one who guided me when I was young’?
‘Is he really going to stay angry forever? Will he hold on to it to the very end?’ Look at you. You said and did evil things and got your own way.”
While Josiah was king, the LORD said to me, “Have you seen what Israel did after turning away? She went up every high mountain and under every leafy tree and sold herself there.
After she did all that, I thought, ‘She’ll come back to me.’ But she didn’t come back, and her two-faced sister Judah saw it.
I saw that even after I sent Israel away with divorce papers for committing adultery, her unfaithful sister Judah wasn’t scared. She went out and sold herself too.
She treated her prostitution like it was no big deal. It dirtied the land, and she cheated with stone and wood.
After all that, her two-faced sister Judah still hasn’t come back to me with her whole heart. She only pretended,” says the LORD.
The LORD told me, “Israel turned away, and even she comes out looking more righteous than two-faced Judah.
Go face north and call this out: ‘Come back, Israel, you who walked away,’ says the LORD. ‘I won’t look at you in anger. I’m merciful,’ says the LORD. ‘I won’t hold on to my anger forever.
Just own what you did. You went against the LORD your God. You chased after strangers all over the place, under every leafy tree, and you didn’t listen to me,’” says the LORD.
“Come back, children who walked away,” says the LORD. “I’m your husband. I’ll take one of you from a city and two from a family, and I’ll bring you to Zion.
I’ll give you shepherds who share my heart. They’ll feed you with knowledge and understanding.

When your numbers grow and you fill the land in those days,” says the LORD, “people won’t say, ‘The ark of the LORD’s covenant!’ anymore. It won’t even cross their minds. They won’t remember it or miss it, and nobody will make another one.
Then they’ll call Jerusalem ‘The LORD’s Throne.’ All the nations will gather in Jerusalem to honor the LORD’s name. They won’t keep following their own stubborn, evil hearts.
In those days, the family of Judah will walk with the family of Israel. Together they’ll leave the land up north and come to the land I gave your ancestors to pass down.

“But I said, ‘How I want to count you among my children and give you a beautiful land, a wonderful inheritance among the armies of the nations!’ I said, ‘You’ll call me “My Father,” and you won’t turn away from following me.’
“But just like a wife who walks out on her husband and betrays him, you betrayed me, family of Israel,” says the LORD.
A sound carries from the bare hills. Israel’s children are crying and begging, because they twisted their own path and forgot the LORD their God.
Come back, you children who wandered off. I’ll heal you of your wandering. “Here we are. We’ve come to you because you’re the LORD our God.
All that noise on the hills and mountains won’t help us. The LORD our God is the one who truly saves Israel.
But ever since we were young, that shameful thing has swallowed up everything our ancestors worked for, their flocks and herds, their sons and daughters.

Let’s lie down in our shame and let disgrace cover us. We’ve sinned against the LORD our God, both we and our ancestors, from the time we were young right up to today. We haven’t listened to the voice of the LORD our God.”
